# rail_link (Resource)

A Link Resilience Unit: one destination URL, shortened by every upstream vendor of the RAIL tier and load-balanced across them.

~> **Links are permanent.** RAIL does not support deleting links, in keeping with industry-standard data retention practices. Destroying this resource removes it from Terraform state only; the link remains provisioned and continues to resolve.

Provisioning is idempotent: a second `rail_link` for the same destination adopts the existing link.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "rail_link" "quarterly_report" {
  url = "https://example.com/q3/synergy-report.pdf"
}

output "short_url" {
  value = rail_link.quarterly_report.short_url
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `url` (String) Destination URL. Changing it to a different destination provisions a new link; a change RAIL normalizes away (host case, a missing root slash) only updates state.

### Read-Only

- `compression_ratio` (Number) Short URL length divided by destination length. Values above 1.0 are expected in multi-tier deployments.
- `created_at` (Number) Unix time the link was provisioned.
- `degraded` (Boolean) True when no mirror is healthy and the tier redirects straight to the destination (Degraded Mode). Observed at the last refresh.
- `id` (String) The link id, as in `<endpoint>/<id>`.
- `mirrors` (Attributes List) One entry per vendor copy of the link, as of the last refresh. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--mirrors))
- `short_url` (String) The short URL to distribute.
- `target` (String) The destination as RAIL normalized it.

<a id="nestedatt--mirrors"></a>
### Nested Schema for `mirrors`

Read-Only:

- `healthy` (Boolean) Whether the mirror is in rotation.
- `short_url` (String) The vendor-issued short URL.
- `upstream` (String) Vendor identifier.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Adopt an existing link by its id (the last path segment of its short URL).
terraform import rail_link.quarterly_report dGJqXvP
```
